text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- More than 1.5 million individuals will pay between 10 and 20 percent less in monthly tax cuts under a revised tax deduction system next year, said Inland Revenue Board executive chairman Mohd Ali Hassan.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has cautioned trade unions and non-governmental organisations against supporting the United States in its attempts to raise non-trade issues at the WTO meeting.
-- The new Kuala Lumpur International Airport will be completed on schedule despite some delays in parts of the project, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
-- Konsortium Perkapalan Bhd and Integrated Logistics Bhd are involved in joint ventures in shipping, trucking and warehousing in the Philippines and Indonesia, industry sources said.
-- Binariang Sdn Bhd has budgeted 800 million ringgit for expansion of its fixed-line services in the coming year, said company chief operating officer Duffy Swan.
-- Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd will undergo a restructuring to provide flexibility in future fund-raising, a company statement said.
-- The Securities Commission has directed Malayan United Industries Bhd to compensate parties who sold shares in Pengkalen Holdings Bhd between April 25 and July 1 this year.
